# http1

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/http1"
```

Package http1 is the restricted HTTP/1.1 profile the SDK serves on its loop engine (ADR 0186 §D6): a codec that frames requests out of bytes and appends responses to bytes, and HandleLoop, the adapter that serves a Handler on a loop group of package server.

It is a profile, not an HTTP server, and what it refuses defines it. A request is answered with its status and Connection: close, and its connection closed, before any handler sees it, when it carries any Transfer-Encoding (chunked, and so trailers, included), Expect, a bare CR or LF, a NUL or another control byte in a value, obs-fold, whitespace before a colon, a name outside tchar, a Content-Length that is not one run of at most ten digits or that repeats, a second Authorization or Host, CONNECT, or a head, target or body past its Limits. HTTP/2, Upgrade and TLS are out of the profile: a program that needs them mounts net/http with Group.HandleHTTP. Framing depends on neither the method nor the route: a request takes its head plus its Content-Length.

### Serving

```
type api struct{ lanes []perLane } // one per lane, indexed by Request.Lane

func (a *api) ServeHTTP1(req *http1.Request, res *http1.Response) {
	l := &a.lanes[req.Lane]
	// route, authenticate with l's own scratch, ...
	res.Defer = true // answered at the end of the batch
	l.pending = append(l.pending, job{res: res})
}

func (a *api) EndBatch(lane int) {
	l := &a.lanes[lane]
	// one transaction for every job of l.pending, then for each:
	// job.res.Status, job.res.Body = ..., ...; job.res.Defer = false
}

srv.Group("api", server.Listen("tcp", ":8080"), server.Loop(server.LoopValue{Loops: 2})).
	HandleLoop(http1.HandleLoop(a, http1.Parser{}))
```

A handler runs on its lane's thread and must not block it. Every callback of one lane runs on that thread, one at a time, so state kept per lane needs no lock; Request.Lane and the lane argument of EndBatch name the lane. The answers of a batch leave at its end, in request order on each connection.

### The codec alone

Parser.Parse, AppendResponse and AppendRefusal frame and write without the loop, on any \[]byte: nothing allocates once the caller's buffers have room.

<a name="HandleLoop"></a>
## func [HandleLoop](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func HandleLoop(h Handler, p Parser) *LoopHandler
```

HandleLoop adapts h to the loop engine: the handler of server.Group.HandleLoop. p frames every request; the zero Parser is the profile's defaults. A refused request is answered and closed without reaching h; the batch's answers leave at its end, after h's EndBatch when h is a Batcher, in request order on each connection. A Response starts every request with a nil Header and Body, which h points at bytes it owns until the answer is taken. An answer the writer refuses, or one left deferred, is answered 500 and its connection closed; one the connection's output refuses closes the connection.


<a name="Parser.Parse"></a>
### func \(Parser\) [Parse](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/parse.go>)

```go
func (Parser) Parse(buf []byte, req *corenet.HTTP1RequestValue) (int, Refusal)
```

Parse frames the request at the start of buf into req and returns the bytes it takes and RefusalNone, once the whole request is there.

It returns 0 and RefusalNone while more bytes are needed. When the head is complete and only the body is missing, req.HeadLen and req.Consumed are already set: Continue then waits for the body without reading the head again, and an early answer knows how much the request still has to send.

It returns 0 and the refusal when the bytes break the profile. A refusal never depends on bytes past the one that broke a rule, so more bytes never turn it into an acceptance; and an accepted request takes the same bytes whatever follows it, the next pipelined request included.

Framing depends on neither the method nor the target: a request takes its head plus its Content-Length, a GET's included. Every slice in req aliases buf. Parse allocates nothing.

```go
type Request struct {
	// Method is the request method, a token.
	Method           []byte
	// Target is the request-target exactly as sent, still percent-encoded.
	Target           []byte
	// Host is the Host field's value; HasHost says whether it was present.
	Host             []byte
	// Authorization is the Authorization field's value; HasAuthorization says
	// whether it was present.
	Authorization    []byte
	// Body is the request content, Content-Length bytes after the head. It is
	// empty until the whole body has arrived.
	Body             []byte
	// ContentLength is the declared body length, zero when the field is absent.
	ContentLength    int64
	// HeadLen is the length of the head: the request line, the field lines and
	// the blank line. It is zero until the head is complete.
	HeadLen          int
	// Consumed is HeadLen plus ContentLength: the bytes this request takes from
	// the stream, whatever its method or route. The next pipelined request
	// starts there. It is set as soon as the head is complete, before the body
	// arrives, so an early answer knows how much it has to drain.
	Consumed         int
	// NFields is how many entries of Fields the request filled.
	NFields          int
	// Fields holds the request's field lines in the order they arrived,
	// Host, Authorization and Content-Length included.
	Fields           [64]HTTP1FieldValue
	// HasHost reports whether the request carried a Host field.
	HasHost          bool
	// HasAuthorization reports whether the request carried an Authorization
	// field.
	HasAuthorization bool
	// Close reports whether the client asked to close the connection after
	// this request: a Connection field holding the close token.
	Close            bool
	// Lane is the index of the lane that framed the request, from 0 to the
	// group's lane count less one — its LoopIO.Loop — set by the loop adapter
	// before the handler runs. One lane is one thread or one goroutine, so a
	// handler finds its per-lane state in a slice sized at LoopStarter.OnStart,
	// with no lock. Parse leaves it as it is; outside the loop adapter it is
	// what the caller set.
	Lane             int
}
```

<a name="Request.Field"></a>
### func \(Request\) [Field](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/net/http1.go>)

```go
func (*Request) Field(name string) ([]byte, bool)
```

Field returns the value of the first field named name and true, or nil and false when the request carries none. Names compare case-insensitively on A–Z only, so no locale or Unicode folding can make two names equal.

<a name="Response"></a>
## type [Response](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

Response is the answer a Handler gives: a status, extra field lines written by AppendField, a body, Close, and Defer to answer at the batch's end.

```go
type Response = corenet.HTTP1ResponseValue
```

Response is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/net.HTTP1ResponseValue`, declared as:

```go
type Response struct {
	// Status is the status code, 200 to 999; zero means 200. The profile
	// sends no interim response.
	Status int
	// Header holds the response's extra field lines, each written as
	// "Name: value\r\n" by the codec's writer. It never holds Content-Length or
	// Connection, which the codec writes.
	Header []byte
	// Body is the response content.
	Body   []byte
	// Close asks the codec to close the connection after this response.
	Close  bool
	// Defer, set by the handler, holds the answer back until the end of the
	// loop's batch, for work it batches — one database transaction for every
	// request of the batch, say. The response value then stays valid, at the
	// same address, until HTTP1Batcher.EndBatch returns, and the handler
	// completes it there: it fills it and clears Defer. An answer still
	// deferred when EndBatch returns is answered 500 and its connection
	// closed. Only the loop adapter reads it; AppendResponse does not.
	Defer  bool
}
```
